topicName: Cell Structure and Organization of Life
description: An introduction to the cell as the basic unit of life, the structures of plant and animal cells and their functions, using the microscope, and how cells are organised into tissues, organs and systems.

mcq.questionText: The basic structural and functional unit of all living things is the:
mcq.explanation: Cells build tissues, which build organs, which build systems, so the cell is the basic unit of life. Exam Tip: Order of organisation: cell to tissue to organ to system to organism.

mcq.questionText: Which instrument is commonly used to study the structure of cells in the school laboratory?
mcq.explanation: Cells are too small for the naked eye or a hand lens, but the light microscope magnifies enough to reveal cell structures. Exam Tip: The light (optical) microscope is standard in schools; the electron microscope is far more powerful but rarely available.

mcq.questionText: Which part of the cell controls all the activities of the cell?
mcq.explanation: The nucleus contains chromosomes made of DNA that direct all cell activities. Exam Tip: Think of the nucleus as the brain or control centre of the cell.

mcq.questionText: Which structure is found in plant cells but ABSENT in animal cells?
mcq.explanation: Nucleus, membrane and cytoplasm occur in both cell types, but the cell wall is unique to plants. Exam Tip: Plant-only structures are the cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole.

mcq.questionText: The part of the plant cell that contains chlorophyll for photosynthesis is the:
mcq.explanation: Chloroplasts hold the green pigment chlorophyll that traps light for photosynthesis. Exam Tip: Chloro means green; chloroplasts are in plant cells, never in animal cells.

mcq.questionText: The structure that controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell is the:
mcq.explanation: The cell (plasma) membrane is selectively permeable, letting some substances pass and blocking others. Exam Tip: The cell wall in plants is fully permeable and gives support, while the cell membrane is selectively permeable and controls entry and exit.

mcq.questionText: The jelly-like fluid in which the cell organelles are suspended is called the:
mcq.explanation: Cytoplasm is the medium that holds the organelles and where many reactions occur. Exam Tip: Most chemical reactions happen in the cytoplasm, the workshop of the cell.

mcq.questionText: The site of respiration where energy is released in the cell is the:
mcq.explanation: Mitochondria carry out respiration, releasing energy for the cell to use. Exam Tip: The mitochondrion is the powerhouse of the cell; the chloroplast traps energy in plants, so do not confuse them.

mcq.questionText: A large permanent vacuole filled with cell sap is a feature of:
mcq.explanation: Mature plant cells have one large, permanent central vacuole filled with cell sap. Exam Tip: The large vacuole stores sap and keeps the plant cell firm (turgid).

mcq.questionText: Which of the following correctly shows the levels of organisation from simplest to most complex?

options.text: Organ to tissue to cell to system
Cell to tissue to organ to system
Tissue to cell to system to organ
System to organ to tissue to cell

mcq.explanation: Start from the cell; similar cells form a tissue, tissues form an organ, and organs form a system. Exam Tip: Build up from the cell; any sequence not starting with the cell is wrong.

mcq.questionText: If the eyepiece lens has a magnification of x10 and the objective lens x40, the total magnification is:
mcq.explanation: Total magnification = eyepiece x objective = 10 x 40 = x400. Exam Tip: Multiply the two lenses, never add; x50 is the add-trap.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a function of the cell wall in plant cells?

options.text: Giving the cell a definite shape

mcq.explanation: The cell wall gives shape, support and protection and is fully permeable, so controlling entry is the membrane's job, not the wall's. Exam Tip: The wall is permeable and lets everything through, so selection belongs to the membrane.

mcq.questionText: The specialisation of cells to perform particular functions is called cell:
mcq.explanation: Cell differentiation is the process by which cells become specialised, for example nerve cells and root hair cells. Exam Tip: Differentiation leads to specialised cells, which form tissues.

mcq.questionText: A root hair cell is long and narrow with a large surface area. This adaptation helps it to:

options.text: Absorb water and mineral salts efficiently

mcq.explanation: A large surface area increases the rate at which the root hair cell absorbs water and mineral salts. Exam Tip: Link structure to function; a large surface area means more absorption.

mcq.questionText: Which type of cell would you expect to have many mitochondria because it needs a lot of energy?
mcq.explanation: Cells that do a lot of work, such as contracting muscle cells, need much energy and so contain many mitochondria. Exam Tip: More activity means more energy means more mitochondria; dead or empty cells need none.

fib.questionText: The three main parts common to both plant and animal cells are the cell membrane, the cytoplasm and the __________.
fib.explanation: The nucleus is present in both plant and animal cells alongside the membrane and cytoplasm. Exam Tip: These three are the universal cell parts.

fib.questionText: The green pigment found in chloroplasts is called __________.
fib.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment inside chloroplasts that traps light for photosynthesis. Exam Tip: Chlorophyll (pigment) sits inside the chloroplast (organelle).

fib.questionText: The part of the cell that stores cell sap in plants is the __________.
fib.explanation: The vacuole stores cell sap in plant cells. Exam Tip: A full vacuole makes the cell turgid; loss of sap makes the plant wilt.

fib.questionText: Total magnification of a microscope is obtained by multiplying the magnification of the eyepiece by that of the __________ lens.
fib.explanation: Total magnification is the eyepiece magnification multiplied by the objective magnification. Exam Tip: Total = eyepiece x objective; the objective is the lens near the specimen.

fib.questionText: A group of similar cells performing the same function is called a __________.
fib.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells that carry out the same function. Exam Tip: The order is cell to tissue to organ to system.

fib.questionText: The structure that gives the plant cell a fixed shape and support is the __________.
fib.explanation: The cell wall gives the plant cell a fixed shape and provides support. Exam Tip: Made of cellulose, the wall keeps plant cells box-like.

fib.questionText: The powerhouse of the cell, where energy is released, is the __________.
fib.explanation: The mitochondrion releases energy through respiration, so it is called the powerhouse of the cell. Exam Tip: Powerhouse of the cell means mitochondrion.

fib.questionText: Organisms whose bodies are made of many cells are said to be __________.
fib.explanation: Organisms made of many cells are described as multicellular. Exam Tip: Examples include humans, trees and most fungi; the opposite is unicellular.

fib.questionText: The process by which cells become specialised to perform particular functions is called cell __________.
fib.explanation: Cell differentiation is the process by which cells become specialised for particular functions. Exam Tip: Do not confuse it with cell division, which makes more cells.

fib.questionText: The selectively permeable structure that surrounds the cytoplasm is the __________.
fib.explanation: The cell membrane is the selectively permeable layer that surrounds the cytoplasm. Exam Tip: Selectively permeable tags the membrane; fully permeable tags the wall.

tf.questionText: The nucleus controls the activities of the cell.
tf.explanation: The nucleus contains DNA that directs and controls all activities of the cell. Exam Tip: The nucleus is the control centre.

tf.questionText: Animal cells have a cell wall made of cellulose.
tf.explanation: A cellulose cell wall is a plant feature; animal cells have only a cell membrane. Exam Tip: The cellulose cell wall is a plant feature; animal cells have only a membrane.

tf.questionText: Chloroplasts are found in both plant and animal cells.
tf.explanation: Only plants and some protists photosynthesise, so chloroplasts are absent from animal cells. Exam Tip: Animals have no chloroplasts.

tf.questionText: The total magnification of a microscope is found by adding the magnification of the two lenses.
tf.explanation: Total magnification is found by multiplying the two lens magnifications, not adding them. Exam Tip: Multiply, not add (10 x 40 = 400).

tf.questionText: A large permanent vacuole is characteristic of mature plant cells.
tf.explanation: Mature plant cells have one large permanent central vacuole filled with sap. Exam Tip: Animal cells may have small temporary vacuoles, not a large permanent one.

tf.questionText: The cell membrane is selectively permeable.
tf.explanation: The cell membrane lets some substances pass while blocking others, so it is selectively permeable. Exam Tip: Selective permeability underlies diffusion and osmosis.

tf.questionText: Cytoplasm is the site where many chemical reactions of the cell take place.
tf.explanation: Many of the cell's chemical reactions occur in the cytoplasm. Exam Tip: The cytoplasm is the cell's workshop.

tf.questionText: All cells in a multicellular organism are identical in structure and function.
tf.explanation: Differentiation produces many different cell types with different structures and functions. Exam Tip: Differentiation produces variety such as nerve, muscle, root hair and blood cells.

tf.questionText: The cell wall is fully (freely) permeable while the cell membrane is selectively permeable.
tf.explanation: The wall lets all substances through while the membrane selects what passes. Exam Tip: Wall means fully permeable plus support; membrane means selectively permeable plus control.

tf.questionText: A sperm cell has a tail to enable it to swim towards the egg.
tf.explanation: The sperm's tail allows it to swim towards the egg, a classic structure-function adaptation. Exam Tip: This is a classic structure-function adaptation.

summary.correctAnswer: The basic structural and functional unit of all living things.
summary.explanation: Cells build up into tissues, organs and systems. Exam Tip: The cell is where the levels of organisation begin.

summary.correctAnswer: The part of the cell that contains DNA and controls all the cell's activities.
summary.explanation: It is found in both plant and animal cells. Exam Tip: Think of the nucleus as the control centre or brain of the cell.

summary.correctAnswer: The jelly-like fluid in which the organelles are suspended and where many reactions occur.
summary.explanation: It fills the cell between the membrane and the nucleus. Exam Tip: The cytoplasm is the workshop of the cell.

summary.correctAnswer: The selectively permeable layer surrounding the cytoplasm that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
summary.explanation: It is present in both plant and animal cells. Exam Tip: Selectively permeable tags the membrane; fully permeable tags the wall.

summary.correctAnswer: A fully permeable cellulose layer outside the membrane of plant cells that gives shape and support.
summary.explanation: It is found in plant cells but not animal cells. Exam Tip: The wall gives support and is fully permeable, unlike the selective membrane.

summary.correctAnswer: The plant-cell organelle containing chlorophyll where photosynthesis takes place.
summary.explanation: Chloroplasts are found only in plant cells. Exam Tip: Chloro means green; chloroplasts trap light energy.

summary.correctAnswer: The organelle where respiration occurs and energy is released, known as the powerhouse of the cell.
summary.explanation: Active cells such as muscle cells contain many mitochondria. Exam Tip: More activity means more mitochondria.

summary.correctAnswer: A fluid-filled space that stores cell sap; large and permanent in mature plant cells.
summary.explanation: A full vacuole keeps a plant cell firm. Exam Tip: A full vacuole makes the cell turgid; loss of sap makes the plant wilt.

summary.correctAnswer: Total magnification = eyepiece magnification x objective magnification.
summary.explanation: For example 10 x 40 gives x400. Exam Tip: Multiply the two lenses, never add.

summary.questionText: Cell to tissue to organ to system
summary.correctAnswer: The levels of organisation from simplest to most complex, starting at the cell.
summary.explanation: Similar cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form systems. Exam Tip: Build up from the cell; any order not starting with the cell is wrong.

hoq.questionText: A student viewed a cell under the microscope and recorded: a cell wall, a large central vacuole, chloroplasts, cytoplasm, a nucleus and a cell membrane. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: It is an animal cell because it has a nucleus
It is a plant cell because it has a cell wall, vacuole and chloroplasts
It is a bacterial cell because it has a cell wall
It cannot be identified from the features given

hoq.explanation: Nucleus, cytoplasm and membrane are universal, while the cell wall, large central vacuole and chloroplasts are all plant-specific, so the cell is a plant cell. Exam Tip: Option A is wrong because the nucleus is in both cell types; identify cells by their diagnostic (unique) features.

hoq.questionText: Under a microscope with a x5 eyepiece, a cell measured 8 mm across when the x10 objective was used. When the student switched to the x40 objective without changing the eyepiece, what happens to the total magnification and the apparent size of the cell?

options.text: Magnification x50 to x200; the cell looks smaller
Magnification x50 to x200; the cell looks 4 times larger
Magnification stays x50; the cell looks the same
Magnification x15 to x45; the cell looks 3 times larger

hoq.explanation: The first total is 5 x 10 = x50, and after switching it is 5 x 40 = x200, an increase factor of 200/50 = 4, so the cell appears 4 times larger. Exam Tip: Option A wrongly says smaller, but higher magnification always makes the specimen look bigger; compute the ratio of magnifications and multiply the lenses, never add.

hoq.questionText: A table shows features seen in three cells. Cell X: cell wall present, chloroplast present, large vacuole present, nucleus present. Cell Y: cell wall absent, chloroplast absent, large vacuole absent (small only), nucleus present. Cell Z: cell wall present, chloroplast absent, large vacuole absent, nucleus present. Which identification of X, Y and Z is correct?

options.text: X = animal, Y = plant, Z = bacterium
X = plant (e.g. leaf), Y = animal, Z = plant root cell
X = bacterium, Y = plant, Z = animal
X = animal, Y = animal, Z = plant

hoq.explanation: X has a wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole so it is a photosynthetic plant cell such as a leaf cell; Y has no wall, no chloroplast and only a small vacuole but a nucleus so it is an animal cell; Z has a wall and nucleus but no chloroplast so it is a plant cell that does not photosynthesise, such as a root cell. Exam Tip: The subtle one is Z; students assume no chloroplast means animal, but Z has a cell wall, which animals never have, and root cells lack chloroplasts because there is no light underground.
